title: The Lexicon
subtitle: Five diamond cuts in one line, read like words in a single sentence.

stone.origin: Twenty-four stones. Eighteen point twenty carats. No two cuts identical. The round brilliant: the most spoken diamond dialect in history — light calculated, faceted, perfected over a century of cutting science. The oval: the round's more elegant sibling, elongating the wrist, softening every room it enters. The pear: tension in silhouette — pointed at one end, yielding at the other. The cut that holds contradiction and makes it beautiful. The emerald: architecture. Still. Direct. The only cut that asks you to look into it, not just at it. The cushion: warmth encoded in geometry — softened corners that carry depth most shapes cannot. Together, they form a sentence. Twenty-four words. One unbroken thought, worn on the wrist.

description: Twenty-four stones, no two cuts identical, gathered into one line. The round brilliant — the most spoken diamond dialect in history, perfected over a century of cutting. The oval — the round elongated, softening every room it enters. The pear — pointed at one end, yielding at the other, contradiction made beautiful. The emerald — architecture, still and direct, the only cut that asks you to look into it. The cushion — warmth encoded in geometry, depth most shapes cannot carry. Set together they form a sentence: twenty-four words, one unbroken thought, worn on the wrist in eighteen-karat white gold.
